reason: The cited evidence does not directly address FeMnNiGeSi alloys or their magnetocaloric response. E1 shows domain wall pinning at grain/twin boundaries in a different alloy system, and E2 shows nanosegregation and exchange bias in Fe2MnAl films, but neither supports the specific claims about pinning broadening ΔSM, hysteresis in magnetocaloric cycles, or the effect of annealing on these properties in the proposed system.
premises: Nanoscale chemical/structural inhomogeneities (secondary phases, defect clusters) exist in as-deposited films
These heterogeneities act as domain wall pinning sites
Pinning broadens the magnetic entropy change distribution and adds hysteresis
Annealing reduces defect density and homogenizes microstructure
Reduced pinning after annealing sharpens ΔSM, reduces hysteresis, and improves refrigerant capacity
